items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: I played at Preservation Hall with him, maybe 20 times. Um, very exciting to play with.

ctx.x: Um, what was your feeling about, was your feeling, how, how many times did you actually play with George Lewis or play with the fans? Many, many times.

I don't, we played a great deal in Japan together with the Japanese. I played at Preservation Hall with him, maybe 20 times. Um, very exciting to play with. And he did something that makes a, uh, a younger musician, not of the same caliber, feel very good. When you played, he listened. And if you made something pretty, he turned around and acknowledged it. Yes, and I think he always was very receptive. He heard. He knew what you were trying to do.

Which I think is something that in some way sets him apart from a lot of the other New Orleans musicians. I mean, I think in that sense George was especially receptive about music. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Well, what, do you find any difference playing with a, uh, say New Orleans Colored Band or a New Orleans Band as opposed to playing with the, the kind of people that you say in Washington? I mean, is there a difference in the music?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: Bob Green passed and healed it. And he saw a sign, and he brought us there.

ctx.x: So, the tours of Japan. Do you have any particular memories? I know this is one story which somebody told me, which I'd like you to repeat if you can remember. It's about this time you went to this place in Tokyo, where they had jukebox with, just with George Lewis records on them. And you went there. And you remember that time? Do you remember that time? Yeah, that was the first year of 63. I remember that.

But they were on the George Lewis record. They were then? They were New York. Yeah. But, now I get, because the very large picture, the large picture from the George Lewis record. Did they know you were coming? No, they didn't know. They knew I was in June, but they didn't know. I was coming to just read that. They didn't know why I went, because, what's the name of John Flair? Bob Green. Bob Green passed and healed it. And he saw a sign, and he brought us there. And, uh, now that I was there, I guess it's an…
How did you like it in Japan in general?
